subproblems.title: Density comparison (Simon 1.3.3) for an arbitrary measure, with the sharp isodiametric constant
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and assume the isodiametric normalisation (IB): μHE[n] ≤ (ω_n/2ⁿ)·μH[n] as measures on ℝ^P = Euclid P. Here ω_n = unitBallVolume n is the volume of the open unit ball of ℝⁿ and μH[n] is Mathlib's unnormalised n-dimensional Hausdorff measure. Let μ be an arbitrary measure on ℝ^P, A ⊆ ℝ^P an arbitrary (not necessarily measurable) set, and t ∈ (0, ∞] such that t < limsup_{r→0+} μ(B̄_r(x))/(ω_n·rⁿ) for every x ∈ A. The quotients are taken in [0, ∞], with ω_n·rⁿ written unitBallVolume n * ofReal(rⁿ). Then t·μHE[n](A) ≤ μ(ℝ^P).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (A : Set (Euclid P)) (t : ℝ≥0∞), (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)) ≤ (unitBallVolume n / 2 ^ n) • (μH[(n : ℝ)] : Measure (Euclid P)) → 0 < t → (∀ x ∈ A, t < limsup (fun r : ℝ => μ (closedBall x r) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0)) → t * μHE[n] A ≤ μ univ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 3 (Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.3 with Lemma 3.4(*) and Corollary 3.5; book/chapter-01.txt lines 602–696). The parent's claim is the special case μ = μHE[n]⌞(M ∩ A₂); the argument below is the parent's argument, written for an arbitrary measure μ. Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n] and ω = ω_n = unitBallVolume n. All quantities lie in [0, ∞], and ediam is the extended diameter. For b = (y, ρ) ∈ ℝ^P × ℝ write B(b) := B̄_ρ(y).
1. Reductions. If μ(ℝ^P) = ∞ the inequality is trivial. If A = ∅ then Hⁿ(A) = 0 and it is again trivial. So assume μ(ℝ^P) < ∞ and fix x₀ ∈ A; then t < (limsup at x₀) ≤ ∞ forces t < ∞. Moreover 0 < ω < ∞, because ω is the volume of the nonempty, open, bounded unit ball of Euclid n (measure_ball_pos, measure_ball_lt_top). Hence 0 < tω < ∞.
2. Fineness. Let x ∈ A and η > 0. Because t < limsup_{r→0+} μ(B̄_r(x))/(ω·ofReal(rⁿ)), the quotient exceeds t frequently as r → 0+ (Filter.frequently_lt_of_lt_limsup; boundedness is automatic in the complete lattice [0, ∞]). Since r ∈ (0, η) eventually (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT), there is ρ ∈ (0, η) with t < μ(B̄_ρ(x))/(ω·ofReal(ρⁿ)). As 0 < ω·ofReal(ρⁿ) < ∞, this is equivalent to t·ω·ofReal(ρ)ⁿ < μ(B̄_ρ(x)) (ENNReal.lt_div_iff_mul_lt, ENNReal.ofReal_pow).
3. Covers at scale δ with slack ε. Fix δ > 0 and ε ∈ (0, ∞], and put D := 2ⁿ·(μ(ℝ^P)/(tω)). We build a countable family (C_b)_{b∈u} such that A ⊆ ⋃_b C_b, ediam C_b ≤ ofReal(5δ) for every b, and Σ_b ediam(C_b)ⁿ ≤ D + ε.
(a) Vitali selection (Simon 3.4(*)). Let T := {(y, ρ) : y ∈ A, 0 < ρ < δ/2, tω·ofReal(ρ)ⁿ < μ(B̄_ρ(y))}. Apply Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement to the family b ↦ B(b) indexed by T, with size function (y, ρ) ↦ ρ, factor τ = 2 and bound R = δ/2. On T the sizes lie in [0, R] and every B(b) is nonempty. This gives u ⊆ T such that the balls B(b), b ∈ u, are pairwise disjoint, and every a = (y, ρ) ∈ T admits some b = (y_b, ρ_b) ∈ u with B(a) ∩ B(b) ≠ ∅ and ρ ≤ 2ρ_b.
(b) Countability. Each B(b), b ∈ u, contains the nonempty open ball B_{ρ_b}(y_b), since ρ_b > 0. A pairwise disjoint family of sets with nonempty interior in the separable space ℝ^P is countable (Set.PairwiseDisjoint.countable_of_nonempty_interior). So u is countable.
(c) Packing. Put s_b := ofReal(ρ_b)ⁿ for b ∈ u. The B(b) are disjoint closed, hence measurable, sets, so tω·Σ_{b∈u} s_b = Σ_{b∈u} tω·s_b ≤ Σ_{b∈u} μ(B(b)) = μ(⋃_{b∈u} B(b)) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) (measure_biUnion). Hence S := Σ_{b∈u} s_b ≤ μ(ℝ^P)/(tω) < ∞.
(d) Finite part. As S < ∞, the tail sums Σ_{b∈u∖F} s_b tend to 0 along the finite subsets F of u ordered by inclusion (ENNReal.tendsto_tsum_compl_atTop_zero). Since ε/10ⁿ > 0, choose a finite F ⊆ u with Σ_{b∈u∖F} s_b < ε/10ⁿ.
(e) The cover. For b ∈ u let C_b := B̄_{ρ_b}(y_b) if b ∈ F, and C_b := B̄_{5ρ_b}(y_b) if b ∉ F.
(f) A ⊆ ⋃_{b∈u} C_b (Simon 3.5). Let x ∈ A. If x ∈ B(b) for some b ∈ F, then x ∈ C_b. Otherwise x lies outside the closed set K := ⋃_{b∈F} B(b), a finite union of closed balls, so there is η > 0 with B_η(x) ∩ K = ∅. By step 2 choose ρ with 0 < ρ < min(η/2, δ/2) and tω·ofReal(ρ)ⁿ < μ(B̄_ρ(x)); then a := (x, ρ) ∈ T. By (a) there are b = (y_b, ρ_b) ∈ u and a point z ∈ B̄_ρ(x) ∩ B(b) with ρ ≤ 2ρ_b. Since d(z, x) ≤ ρ < η, z ∈ B_η(x), so z ∉ K; as z ∈ B(b), this forces b ∉ F. Finally d(x, y_b) ≤ d(x, z) + d(z, y_b) ≤ ρ + ρ_b ≤ 3ρ_b ≤ 5ρ_b, so x ∈ B̄_{5ρ_b}(y_b) = C_b.
(g) Diameters. A closed ball of radius r has extended diameter ≤ ofReal(2r), by ediam_le_of_forall_dist_le and the triangle inequality. Hence ediam C_b ≤ ofReal(10ρ_b) ≤ ofReal(5δ), because ρ_b < δ/2. Moreover ediam(C_b)ⁿ ≤ (2·ofReal ρ_b)ⁿ = 2ⁿ·s_b when b ∈ F, and ediam(C_b)ⁿ ≤ (10·ofReal ρ_b)ⁿ = 10ⁿ·s_b when b ∉ F. (Mathlib's Hausdorff sums use the real exponent (n : ℝ); x^(n:ℝ) = xⁿ by ENNReal.rpow_natCast.)
(h) Cost. By (g), ediam(C_b)ⁿ ≤ 2ⁿ·s_b + 1_{b∉F}·10ⁿ·s_b for every b ∈ u. Sum this over u, using ENNReal.tsum_add and ENNReal.tsum_mul_left, and tsum_subtype to turn the indicator sum into a sum over {b ∈ u : b ∉ F}. This gives Σ_{b∈u} ediam(C_b)ⁿ ≤ 2ⁿ·S + 10ⁿ·Σ_{b∈u∖F} s_b ≤ 2ⁿ·μ(ℝ^P)/(tω) + 10ⁿ·(ε/10ⁿ) = D + ε (ENNReal.mul_div_cancel, using 0 < 10ⁿ < ∞).
4. Hausdorff measure. Let ε > 0. For each k ∈ ℕ apply step 3 with δ_k := 1/(k+1) and this ε, obtaining countable families (C^k_b)_{b∈u_k}. Then r_k := ofReal(5/(k+1)) → 0, ediam C^k_b ≤ r_k for all b, every family covers A, and Σ_b ediam(C^k_b)ⁿ ≤ D + ε for every k. By Measure.hausdorffMeasure_le_liminf_tsum (index set ℕ with the filter atTop, countable index types u_k), μH[n](A) ≤ liminf_k Σ_b ediam(C^k_b)ⁿ ≤ D + ε (liminf_le_of_frequently_le'). Since ε > 0 is arbitrary, μH[n](A) ≤ D = 2ⁿ·μ(ℝ^P)/(tω) (ENNReal.le_of_forall_pos_le_add).
5. Normalisation. (IB) holds setwise for every subset of ℝ^P, measurable or not (Measure.le_iff'; (c•ν)(A) = c·ν(A) by Measure.smul_apply). Hence Hⁿ(A) ≤ (ω/2ⁿ)·μH[n](A) ≤ (ω/2ⁿ)·2ⁿ·(μ(ℝ^P)/(tω)) = ω·(μ(ℝ^P)/(tω)) (ENNReal.div_mul_cancel, using 0 < 2ⁿ < ∞). Multiplying by t gives t·Hⁿ(A) ≤ tω·(μ(ℝ^P)/(tω)) = μ(ℝ^P) (ENNReal.mul_div_cancel, using 0 < tω < ∞). ∎

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 4 (Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.26(1); book/chapter-01.txt lines 1197–1215). Simon 3.3 is supplied by the sibling density_comparison (Lean: Submission.cbr_ci_gp_density_comparison). Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n], ω = unitBallVolume n, Θ*(x) := limsup_{r→0+} Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(x))/(ω·ofReal(rⁿ)) ∈ [0, ∞], and ν₀ := μHE[n].restrict M.
1. Preliminaries. ν₀(ℝ^P) = Hⁿ(M) < ∞, so ν₀ is a finite Borel measure on the metric space ℝ^P (isFiniteMeasure_restrict). Finite Borel measures on metric spaces are weakly regular, in particular outer regular, so Set.exists_isOpen_lt_of_lt applies to ν₀ and to arbitrary, not necessarily measurable, sets. Since M is measurable, ν₀(S) = Hⁿ(S ∩ M) for every S ⊆ ℝ^P (Measure.restrict_apply').
2. Superlevel sets are null. Let t ∈ [0, ∞] with 1 < t < ∞. Put A_t := {x ∈ M : t < Θ*(x)} and a := Hⁿ(A_t) ≤ Hⁿ(M) < ∞.
(a) We show t·a ≤ a + ε for every ε > 0. Since ν₀(A_t) = Hⁿ(A_t ∩ M) = a < a + ε, outer regularity gives an open U ⊇ A_t with ν₀(U) = Hⁿ(U ∩ M) < a + ε (Measure.restrict_apply, as the open set U is measurable).
(b) Put μ' := μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ U) and let x ∈ A_t. Then x ∈ U, so B_η(x) ⊆ U for some η > 0 (Metric.isOpen_iff). For 0 < r < η, B̄_r(x) ⊆ B_η(x) ⊆ U, hence μ'(B̄_r(x)) = Hⁿ(B̄_r(x) ∩ (M ∩ U)) = Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(x)) (Measure.restrict_apply; closed balls are measurable). So the functions r ↦ μ'(B̄_r(x))/(ω·ofReal(rⁿ)) and r ↦ Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(x))/(ω·ofReal(rⁿ)) agree eventually in 𝓝[>]0, and their limsups coincide (Filter.limsup_congr). Therefore t < Θ*(x) = limsup_{r→0+} μ'(B̄_r(x))/(ω·ofReal(rⁿ)).
(c) By (b), density_comparison applies to the measure μ', the set A_t and the constant t (0 < 1 < t), together with (IB). It gives t·a = t·Hⁿ(A_t) ≤ μ'(ℝ^P) = Hⁿ(M ∩ U) = Hⁿ(U ∩ M) < a + ε (Measure.restrict_apply_univ).
(d) By (a)–(c) and ENNReal.le_of_forall_pos_le_add, t·a ≤ a. If a ≠ 0 then, since a ≠ ∞ and 1 < t, a = a·1 < a·t = t·a (ENNReal.mul_lt_mul_right), a contradiction. Hence Hⁿ(A_t) = a = 0.
3. The exceptional set. Let x ∈ M with 1 < Θ*(x). Then Θ*(x) − 1 ≠ 0, so k⁻¹ < Θ*(x) − 1 for some k ∈ ℕ (ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt). Since (k+1)⁻¹ ≤ k⁻¹, the number t_k := 1 + (k+1)⁻¹ satisfies t_k < Θ*(x) (lt_tsub_iff_right), and every t_k satisfies 1 < t_k < ∞. Therefore {x ∈ M : 1 < Θ*(x)} ⊆ ⋃_{k∈ℕ} A_{t_k}, which by step 2 is a countable union of Hⁿ-null sets. Hence Hⁿ({x ∈ M : 1 < Θ*(x)}) = 0 (measure_iUnion_null, measure_mono_null).
4. Conclusion. ν₀({a : ¬(Θ*(a) ≤ 1)}) = Hⁿ({a : 1 < Θ*(a)} ∩ M) = 0 (Measure.restrict_apply', not_le). That is, Θ*(a) ≤ 1 for ν₀-almost every a (ae_iff). ∎

Source: parent proof, steps 5–6 (Besicovitch differentiation with closed balls, then normalisation by ω_nrⁿ). This proof uses the lintegral form of the differentiation theorem that step 5 names (VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_lintegral_enorm_sub_div). In place of the bound Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a)) ≤ 2ω_nrⁿ it uses any finite eventual bound C on the density quotient. Notation: Hⁿ = μHE[n], ω = unitBallVolume n, ν₀ := μHE[n].restrict M. For a point a and r > 0 put I(r) := ∫⁻_{M∩B̄_r(a)} ‖τ(x) − τ(a)‖ₑ dHⁿ(x), m(r) := Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a)) and w(r) := ω·ofReal(rⁿ).
1. Integrability. ν₀(ℝ^P) = Hⁿ(M) < ∞, so ν₀ is a finite (hence s-finite and locally finite) Borel measure (isFiniteMeasure_restrict). τ is strongly measurable and ∫⁻ ‖τ‖ₑ dν₀ = ∫⁻_M ‖τ‖ₑ dHⁿ < ∞, so τ has finite integral. Hence τ is ν₀-integrable, in particular locally integrable, as a map into the normed space MultiVector P n. (Formalisation note: with the default instances the proposition `Integrable τ ν₀` does not elaborate for MultiVector P n, because no ContinuousENorm instance is found for the strong topology of Covector (Euclid P) n →L[ℝ] ℝ. Pass the integrability directly as the argument of the differentiation lemma with `(E := MultiVector P n)`, namely `Integrable.locallyIntegrable ⟨hτ.aestronglyMeasurable, hfin⟩`. This typechecks because the strong topology and the norm topology are definitionally equal.)
2. Differentiation. Euclid P is a finite-dimensional normed space, so it has the Besicovitch covering property and v := Besicovitch.vitaliFamily ν₀ is a Vitali family for ν₀. By VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_lintegral_enorm_sub_div, for ν₀-almost every a, (∫⁻_E ‖τ(y) − τ(a)‖ₑ dν₀(y))/ν₀(E) → 0 as E → v.filterAt a. By Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt ν₀ a, B̄_r(a) → v.filterAt a as r → 0+. Composing the two limits, (∫⁻_{B̄_r(a)} ‖τ − τ(a)‖ₑ dν₀)/ν₀(B̄_r(a)) → 0 as r → 0+. Fix such an a; we prove the implication at a.
3. Rewriting. Closed balls are measurable, so (ν₀)⌞B̄_r(a) = Hⁿ⌞(B̄_r(a) ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict) and ν₀(B̄_r(a)) = Hⁿ(B̄_r(a) ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_apply). Using B̄_r(a) ∩ M = M ∩ B̄_r(a), step 2 says q(r) := I(r)/m(r) → 0 as r → 0+.
4. Bounded density. Assume limsup_{r→0+} m(r)/w(r) < ∞ and choose C with limsup m/w < C < ∞ (exists_between). Then m(r)/w(r) < C for all r in some set belonging to 𝓝[>]0 (Filter.eventually_lt_of_limsup_lt).
5. Comparison. Let r > 0 with m(r)/w(r) < C. If m(r) = 0, the integral over the null set M ∩ B̄_r(a) vanishes (setLIntegral_measure_zero), so I(r)/w(r) = 0 ≤ C·q(r). subproblems.title: θζ is strongly measurable with finite ∫_M‖θζ‖ when |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α|_E
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on ℝ^P and M ⊆ ℝ^P measurable. Let θ : ℝ^P → ℝ be measurable with θ > 0 on M and ∫⁻_M ofReal(θ) dμ < ∞. Let ζ : ℝ^P → MultiVector P n be strongly measurable with |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm(α) for every x ∈ ℝ^P and every n-covector α. Then x ↦ θ(x)•ζ(x) is strongly measurable and ∫⁻_M ‖θ(x)•ζ(x)‖ₑ dμ(x) < ∞, where ‖·‖ is the operator norm on MultiVector P n.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (θ : Euclid P → ℝ) (ζ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), MeasurableSet M → Measurable θ → StronglyMeasurable ζ → (∀ x ∈ M, 0 < θ x) → ∫⁻ x in M, ENNReal.ofReal (θ x) ∂μ < ∞ → (∀ (x : Euclid P) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), |ζ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → StronglyMeasurable (fun x => θ x • ζ x) ∧ ∫⁻ x in M, ‖θ x • ζ x‖ₑ ∂μ < ∞
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 1–2 (bounded field; integrability of τ = θζ). Notation: e_1, …, e_P is the standard orthonormal basis (EuclideanSpace.basisFun). ‖·‖ denotes the operator norms on Covector (Euclid P) n (continuous alternating n-linear forms) and on MultiVector P n = (Covector (Euclid P) n →L[ℝ] ℝ). Put C := √(card(Fin n → Fin P)) = √(Pⁿ) ≥ 0.
1. Measurability. θ is a measurable real function, hence strongly measurable, and ζ is strongly measurable. So x ↦ θ(x)•ζ(x) is strongly measurable (StronglyMeasurable.smul).
2. Coefficient norm versus operator norm. Let α be an n-covector. For every I : Fin n → Fin P, |α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)})| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_i ‖e_{I(i)}‖ = ‖α‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm; ‖e_j‖ = 1). Now covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} [StrictMono I]·α(e_I)²), and each summand is ≤ ‖α‖²; the summands with I not strictly increasing are 0. Summing over the card(Fin n → Fin P) indices and using monotonicity of √ (Real.sqrt_le_sqrt, Real.sqrt_mul, Real.sqrt_sq) gives covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ √(card·‖α‖²) = C·‖α‖.
3. Bounded field. For every x and α, |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ C·‖α‖. As C ≥ 0, ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound gives ‖ζ(x)‖ ≤ C.
4. Pointwise bound on M. Let x ∈ M, so θ(x) > 0. Scalar multiplication of continuous linear maps is pointwise, (c•f)(α) = c·f(α). Hence for every α, |(θ(x)•ζ(x))(α)| = θ(x)·|ζ(x)(α)| ≤ θ(x)·C·‖α‖, and opNorm_le_bound gives ‖θ(x)•ζ(x)‖ ≤ C·θ(x). (Formalisation note: argue through opNorm_le_bound rather than norm_smul or enorm_smul, because the instances NormSMulClass ℝ (MultiVector P n) and ENormSMulClass ℝ (MultiVector P n) are not found with the default instances.) Therefore ‖θ(x)•ζ(x)‖ₑ = ofReal ‖θ(x)•ζ(x)‖ ≤ ofReal(C)·ofReal(θ(x)) (ofReal_norm; ENNReal.ofReal_mul, as C ≥ 0).
5. Integral bound. M is measurable and the bound of step 4 holds at every point of M (setLIntegral_mono'). Hence ∫⁻_M ‖θ•ζ‖ₑ dμ ≤ ∫⁻_M ofReal(C)·ofReal(θ) dμ = ofReal(C)·∫⁻_M ofReal(θ) dμ (lintegral_const_mul, since x ↦ ofReal(θ(x)) is measurable). This is < ∞ because ofReal(C) < ∞ and ∫⁻_M ofReal(θ) dμ < ∞ by hypothesis (ENNReal.mul_lt_top). Together with step 1 this is the claim. ∎
